```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
                      warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5,
                      fig.align = "center", dpi = 72, fig.retina = 1, dev = "png", out.width = "100%")
```

This guide walks through one survey on Island X, from the fishery to the
estimate, and then judges the design by repeating it. Every step is a plain
function; the app (`run_app()`) calls the same functions.

# 1. The island

```{r island}
library(casimir)
fish <- cas_fishery(island_x(), seed = 1)
fish
```

```{r map, fig.height = 6}
plot(fish)
```

::: {.info}
**The population.** `fish$landings` holds every trip: site, date, segment,
hours fished, landing hour and the true landed weight of each species. The
survey runs in the last year; its true catch is the answer key.
:::

```{r truth}
truth <- cas_truth(fish, years = max(fish$years), by = "year")
truth[order(-truth$kg), c("species", "kg")]
```

# 2. The frame survey

```{r frame}
frame <- frame_survey(fish)
frame
```

# 3. A design

Six site-days per site type and quarter, three landings per segment at each
visit, a 10 kg subsample from each.

```{r design}
d <- cas_design(m = 6, n = 3, w_kg = 10, name = "A")
d
design_cost(d, fishery = fish)
```

# 4. Roll: the field forms

```{r roll}
s <- draw_sample(fish, d, seed = 2)
s
head(s$A)   # Form A: landings counted at each visit, by segment
head(s$B)   # Form B: sampled landings
head(s$C)   # Form C: species weights in the subsamples
```

```{r grid, fig.height = 5}
plot_design_grid(s, "Beach", quarter = 1)
```

# 5. Raise

```{r raise}
e <- estimate_catch(s)
e
```

The intermediate steps are kept: `e$landing` (step 1), `e$psu` (step 2) and
`e$stratum` (step 3).

```{r estimate-plot, fig.height = 5}
plot_estimate(e, fish)
```

# 6. Spin: is the design any good?

::: {.predict}
**Predict.** Which species will have the largest CV? Will the 95% intervals
contain the true catch 95% of the time?
:::

```{r spin, fig.height = 6}
ev <- replicate_design(fish, d, R = 100, seed = 3)
ev
plot_eval(ev)
```

::: {.info}
**Reading the result.** The bias is close to zero for every species: the
estimators are unbiased. The CV is small for the main species and large for
rare ones. Coverage is below 0.95 for species with skewed catches, because
six site-days per stratum give a poor estimate of the variance.
:::

# 7. Cash out

```{r cashout, eval = FALSE}
export_survey(s, dir = "survey_A")                      # for trainees
export_survey(s, dir = "survey_A_key", answer_key = fish) # with the answer key
```
